title: CRD watering rules: lawn days, times and new sod

seo.title: CRD watering rules: lawn days, times and new sod
seo.description: CRD Stage 1 lawn watering days and times for Greater Victoria, the new sod schedule, and how to set an irrigation timer to match, with the CRD source.

summary: A plain-language summary of the Capital Regional District's summer watering schedule for lawns, gardens and new sod.

body.p: Most properties in Greater Victoria get their water from the regional supply run by the Capital Regional District (CRD). From May 1 to September 30, Stage 1 watering rules set when lawns can be watered. Properties on private wells are not on the regional supply.

list: Times: 4 am to 10 am, or 7 pm to 10 pm.
Multi-unit complexes, such as stratas, use the complex's street address, not each unit's number.

body.p: Under Stage 1, hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and flower and vegetable gardens is allowed on any day. That is one reason we often convert beds from spray heads to drip.
New sod or seed does not need a permit and has its own temporary watering schedule. Check the CRD page for the current details before you lay new lawn.
In a dry year the CRD can move to a higher stage with tighter limits. Check the CRD site during summer for the current stage.

list: Set the lawn zones to your two allowed days and to start inside the allowed window.
Run several shorter cycles rather than one long one on slopes, so water soaks in instead of running off.
Set drip zones separately; they are not tied to lawn days under Stage 1.
Add a rain or soil-moisture sensor so the system skips wet days.

body.p: Need your system set up or adjusted? See [irrigation services](/services/irrigation/), our [spring checklist](/resources/spring-lawn-and-garden-checklist/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/).
Rules change. Check the official source linked below before you act; this summary was prepared in November 2026.
